exam_scheme.note: Sikkim Teacher Eligibility Test (STET) is conducted annually by the Examination Section, Education Department, Government of Sikkim, Tashiling Secretariat, Gangtok, in coordination with the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT), Sikkim, under Section 23(1) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 and National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) statutory norms. In alignment with NEP 2020 recommendations, the curriculum was revamped in academic collaboration with Azim Premji University, contextualizing the assessment to state pedagogical needs. The examination comprises two distinct pen-and-paper OMR objective tests conducted on the same day: Paper I (for Primary Teachers of Classes I to V) and Paper II (for Graduate / Elementary Teachers of Classes VI to VIII). Each paper features 150 Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) carrying 1 mark each with no negative marking across a 150-minute (2 hours 30 minutes) duration. Language I is compulsory English (medium of instruction), while Language II is chosen by the candidate from among the five vernacular languages taught in Sikkim schools: Nepali, Bhutia, Lepcha, Limboo, or Hindi. The minimum qualifying threshold is 60% (90/150) for unreserved candidates and 55% (82/150) for SC, ST, Central OBC, and State OBC candidates. In accordance with amended NCTE guidelines adopted by the Government of Sikkim, the STET Certificate carries lifetime validity.

competition_benchmarks.note: Official qualification statistics, registered candidate cohorts, and cycle notifications compiled directly from gazettes and official result releases published by the Examination Section, Education Department, Government of Sikkim and Sikkim State Teachers' Recruitment Board (SSTRB). STET is a statutory qualifying eligibility examination under NCTE norms and does not carry recruitment vacancies or mains selection stages.
